brief.essentiel: Agon , a London-based defence AI startup building sovereign infrastructure for autonomous military systems, has raised a €63.87 million ($70 million) Series A round at a valuation of €411.3 million ($450 million).
points: At the Budget, the Chancellor announced an additional £140 million for the Sovereign AI Fund, which will back promising early-stage AI companies with a meaningful UK presence.
The UK Government’s Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF) also joined the round, marking their first joint investment.
The raise brings Agon’s total raised to date to €94.1 million ($100 million), following its emergence from stealth earlier this year with €28 million in Seed capital.
The round was led by Northzone with participation from returning investors Lakestar, XYZ, Lux Capital, and Global Founders Capital.

brief.essentiel: coprod , a Swiss robotics hardware startup building modular hardware components for robotics and physical AI applications, has raised €5.45 million ($6 million) in a pre-Seed funding round.
points: With specialised actuators, sensors, and control systems required for humanoid robotics applications slated to become a $28 billion market by 2030, according to McKinsey, coprod is targeting a market with substantial opportunity.

The round was co-led by Founderful and PROTOTYPE, with additional backing from General Catalyst, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures, SDAC, Unruly Capital, and Venturekick.
Angel investors also participated, including Thomas Wolf, founder of Hugging Face; the Dassault Family; Florent Perrichon; and other renowned angels.
“ The robotics revolution is real and we will be able to rethink every industry because of it. coprod is fixing the biggest problem in hardware: integration hell.

articles.title: Theseus Robotics secures €455k to put robots to work in supermarkets across Europe and US

brief.essentiel: Theseus Robotics , a Swiss startup developing AI-powered robots to automate shelf restocking and online grocery order picking, has secured €455k ($500k) from Y Combinator and will be launching in a grocery store in Silicon Valley.
points: Paris-based Bleu Robotics secured €5 million to develop humanoid learning software, while Inbolt raised €11 million for robot vision and intelligence.
Closer to home, Swiss Physical AI companies Enact Intelligence and Exclaim Robotics secured €26.68 million and €4.29 million respectively, with mutual investor Founderful co-leading Exclaim’s round.

The investment follows earlier backing from Founderful Campus, S2S Ventures, Earthling VC and Berlin-based Caesar Ventures, as the company prepares to introduce its robot, Theo, into its first grocery stores in the EU and US in November 2026.
In warehouse automation, Poland’s Nomagic raised €8.3 million and Germany’s Sereact secured €93 million.

articles.title: OPINION: AI will favour the companies built for AI, not adapted to it

brief.essentiel: For decades, business leaders have been warned that the impending arrival of a new technology will completely reorder the corporate world.
points: But for the best part of the last thirty years, it did not.
With AI, however, the warning deserves more consideration.
The web, mobile phones, cloud computing and social media, for example, were all predicted as disruptors that would sweep the incumbents aside.
The reason is less to do with the technology itself, but rather who is best placed to use it, and that is increasingly becoming startups, rather than established companies.

articles.title: Is Silicon Valley turning its back on Europe? Plug and Play’s Thomas Bigagli weighs in

brief.essentiel: Sequoia Capital’s decision to close its London office has reignited debate about the future of European innovation and the commitment of US investors to the continent – especially amid other departures including Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue.
points: However, not all US investors in Europe share this gloomy outlook.
